newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MP blasts government's economic policy.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MP blasts government's economic policy.

text.p: Kuwait's parliament speaker warned that government privatisation policies could cause an economic catastrophe and a security problem, newspapers reported on Sunday.
Ahmad al-Saadoun, speaking in parliament, charged that "influential" Kuwaitis were benefiting from a lack of regulations on a privatisation programme launched in 1994.

"Can we continue with the privatisation policy without rules?" al-Seyassah newspaper quoted Saadoun as saying. Current practices are "pushing towards concentrating the whole state in the hands of a small group of people."
Previous privatisation operations offered equal opportunities to individual and institutional investors through auctions and public subscriptions, officials say.

The state has sold stakes in 22 listed and unlisted firms for 740 million dinars ($2.4 billion) since the launch of the first phase of the programme in September 1994. Shares worth another one billion dinars are to be sold by the end of 1998.
"Should this continue, the consequences would be an economic catastrophe and a major security problem," Arab Times daily quoted the speaker as saying.

Some officials and leading MPs have said parliament could pass in its current session to the end of June a bill governing privatisation of state utilities. But Saadoun said parliament should block the process if the house was not allowed to regulate it.
The bill includes regulations to monitor price levels and compensate and subsidise Kuwaiti workers in the public sector service firms earmarked for privatisation.
